conventions: Formatting is Prettier via @excalidraw/prettier-config (2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas, 80 columns); eslint reports prettier/prettier as a warning and runs with --max-warnings=0, so every file must be prettier-clean.
Import order (eslint import/order, enforced): builtin, external, then @excalidraw/** packages, then parent/sibling relative imports, with all `import type` lines last; a blank line between groups.
Type-only imports use a separate `import type { ... }` statement (consistent-type-imports, separate-type-imports style).

Inside packages/element import sibling modules relatively ("./textStyleRanges"); packages/excalidraw imports element code from "@excalidraw/element" and element types from "@excalidraw/element/types"; non-test files in packages/excalidraw never import from the "@excalidraw/excalidraw" barrel or ".."/"../index".
jotai is imported only through packages/excalidraw/editor-jotai.ts (atom, editorJotaiStore, useAtomValue), never from "jotai" directly.
Elements are immutable data: change them only through newElementWith(element, updates) or scene.mutateElement(element, updates); never assign to element fields.
DOM access in packages/excalidraw goes through the editor's ownerDocument/ownerWindow (or svgRoot.ownerDocument), never the global document/window.
TypeScript strict: no `any`, no non-null assertions on values that can be null at runtime; new public types are exported type aliases with a JSDoc line.
Every style-range offset is a UTF-16 code-unit index into `originalText`, `start` inclusive and `end` exclusive; the wrapped `text` is never indexed by a range.
UI strings are i18n keys rendered with t("labels.<key>"); keys are added to packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json only; no literal text in JSX.
Comments are short and say why, in the repo's lower-case comment voice; keep existing comments of edited code intact.

Tests run on vitest with globals (describe/it/expect; import `vi` from "vitest" only when mocking), jsdom and vitest-canvas-mock, where a text's measured width equals its string length in px; unit tests build elements with API.createElement from @excalidraw/excalidraw/tests/helpers/api and add style ranges with newElementWith; editor tests render <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} /> and read state from window.h.

decisions.choice: ExcalidrawTextElement gains `styleRanges?: readonly TextStyleRange[]`, where `TextStyleRange = Readonly<{ start: number; end: number; color?: string; highlight?: string }>`; `color` is the text colour, `highlight` the background colour; a stored range never carries a key whose value is undefined.
decisions.reason: Flat optional keys serialise compactly and offsets into originalText survive every re-wrap (FR-1, FR-10).

decisions.choice: A never-styled text has no `styleRanges` key at all; clearing the last range writes `styleRanges: []`; every reader tests `element.styleRanges?.length`; restore turns an empty or invalid array back into no key.
decisions.reason: mutateElement and newElementWith skip undefined values, so a key cannot be unset through them, and plain text must serialise exactly as today (NFR-1).

decisions.choice: An editor-jotai atom `textEditorSelectionAtom` in packages/excalidraw/actions/colorTargets.ts holds `{ elementId, start, end } | null`; textWysiwyg writes it through editorJotaiStore, the colour actions read it with editorJotaiStore.get in perform and useAtomValue in their PanelComponents; AppState and appState.ts are not changed.
rejected: a plain module variable without subscribers
decisions.reason: FR-20 only asks for app state if needed; the atom re-renders the colour panels on selection change without touching the persisted/collaborated state or the full-appState snapshots in history, regression and contextmenu tests.

decisions.topic: Where ranges are shifted while typing
decisions.choice: textWysiwyg.tsx shifts the edited element's styleRanges itself, in its input handler before onChange, with scene.mutateElement(..., { informMutation: false, isDragging: false }); it keeps `styleRangesText`, the text the ranges are aligned to, and indent/outdent pre-shift one edit per tab and update that text so the input event that follows finds nothing to shift.
decisions.reason: App.text.ts is outside the allowlist and spreads the latest scene element, so ranges mutated just before onChange land in the same update; refreshTextDimensions cannot tell wrapped from original text.

decisions.choice: getStyledLines(originalText, text, ranges) aligns each wrapped line of `text` to `originalText` by string matching (a hard newline is stepped over once, whitespace dropped at a soft break is skipped), with no font measurement; textWrapping.ts and textMeasurements.ts are not edited.
decisions.reason: Pure and measurement-free (NFR-3), and it maps exactly what was drawn, so stored ranges never change on re-wrap (FR-6, FR-10, FR-11).

decisions.choice: Canvas and SVG both measure each run with getLineWidth(run.text, getFontString(element), renderEnvironment) and place runs with getStyledRunPositions(widths, element.textAlign, element.width, isRTL(element.text)); an RTL line lays its runs right to left from the line's right edge.
rejected: context.measureText on canvas and a different measure in SVG
decisions.reason: FR-28 requires both outputs to use the same measurement; one pure positioning helper keeps canvas and SVG highlights identical.

decisions.topic: Colour semantics of a range pick
decisions.choice: A stroke pick on a non-empty editor selection that is not the whole text (a whole-text selection, which Enter-to-edit auto-selects, recolours the element as today; for a background pick this exception holds only on sticky-note labels, whose pick colours the note) applies `{ color }`, or `{ color: null }` when the colour equals the element's strokeColor; a background pick applies `{ highlight }`, or `{ highlight: null }` when isTransparent(color); the pick returns only the changed text element and `{ ...appState, ...appStateUpdates }` with CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY and never writes strokeColor, backgroundColor, a container or a currentItem default.
decisions.reason: Gate 1 resolved question 1 and FR-21 to FR-24.

decisions.choice: When a range is selected and canChangeBackgroundColor (components/shapeActionPredicates.ts) is false for the edited text, the stroke-colour PanelComponent also renders renderAction("changeBackgroundColor") below its picker; sticky-note labels already show the background picker and get no second one.
decisions.reason: Both files are outside the allowlist, and the background picker is hidden for free and bound text today, yet FR-21/FR-23 need a highlight pick.

decisions.choice: actionStyles.ts and data/reconcile.ts are not edited; FR-26 and FR-17 are pinned by tests.
decisions.reason: actionPasteStyles writes an explicit list of style keys that excludes styleRanges, and reconciliation already keeps the winning element whole, text and ranges together.

decisions.choice: ExcalidrawElementWithCanvas records `styleRanges` (the element's array reference, or null) and generateElementWithCanvas regenerates when it differs.
rejected: relying on a new element object per change
decisions.reason: An in-place scene.mutateElement of styleRanges keeps the WeakMap key, so the reference must be part of the cache key (FR-14).

decisions.choice: sanitizeStyleRanges(value, textLength): a non-array gives null; an entry is dropped unless it is an object with integer start and end; a colour key is kept only when it is a non-empty string; an entry with no colour key left is dropped; start and end are clamped into [0, textLength]; start >= end is dropped; the rest is normalised; an empty result gives null and restore deletes the key.
decisions.reason: FR-15/FR-16 with one exact rule set the tests can pin.

decisions.choice: labels.rangeTextColor = "Selected text color" and labels.rangeHighlight = "Selected text highlight"; they replace the stroke/background picker labels (and full-mode headings) while a range is selected.
decisions.reason: FR-25 asks the panel to tell a range pick from an element pick.
